correctness.rationale: Under Beta(alpha,beta) latent prevalence, Q_k=(beta)_k/(kappa)_k and C_k=1/k+1-Q_k (k>=2, C_1=1). First differences have sign H_k-1, H_k=alpha k(k+1)Q_k/(kappa+k), with H_(k+1)/H_k=(k+2)(kappa+k-alpha)/[k(kappa+k+1)]. For alpha<1 this strictly exceeds 1, and gamma-ratio asymptotic makes H_k→∞. Thus the first H_k>=1 is the finite global optimum (possible adjacent tie); alpha<1 gives C_k<1 eventually, beating singleton. For alpha=kappa p→0, uniformly for k~t/alpha, log Q_k=-alpha(log k-psi(kappa))+o(alpha), so H_(floor(t/alpha))→t, alpha K_p→1 and min C=alpha[log(1/alpha)+1-psi(kappa)]+o(alpha). Independent exact-rational finite differences and global minimizers in three parameter pairs corroborated. Infinite p→0 follows from uniform logarithmic expansion.
